summary: Full backend + frontend test of CircuitWorks owner dashboard (JWT auth at /admin), booking APIs and public landing page. Backend: 20 pytest cases (19 pass / 1 fail) covering login, /auth/me, /auth/refresh, logout, brute force, booking create/list/patch, auth guards, validation and persistence. Frontend: Playwright on the preview URL covering landing render, booking submit (201 + success state), footer owner-login link, invalid login error, valid login -> dashboard, filter tabs + counts, mark handled / reopen with reload persistence, refresh button, logout + revisit /admin, plus a 390px mobile pass. Only real defect found: brute-force lockout is ineffective through the public ingress. Owner alert email confirmed in backend log (Emergent email proxy 202 Accepted, 'Booking alert email sent to owner').

critical.issue: Brute-force lockout does NOT trigger via the public URL. Identifier is f'{request.client.host}:{email}', and request.client.host is the ingress pod IP; the cluster has multiple ingress replicas (observed login_attempts docs for 10.79.139.10:<email> count=5 and 10.79.139.11:<email> count=1), so the counter is split and 6+ wrong passwords still return 401 instead of 429. Confirmed the logic itself works when hitting localhost:8001 directly (6th attempt = 429). Fix: key the counter on the normalised email (optionally combined with the first hop of X-Forwarded-For), not on request.client.host.

minor.issue: CORS_ORIGINS is '*' while allow_credentials=True and cookies are SameSite=None; Secure. Starlette reflects the caller origin, so ANY site can make credentialed calls to the protected /api/bookings endpoints (CSRF-style risk). Playbook requires explicit origins.

delete_cookie() is called without secure=True/samesite='none' (mismatch with how the cookies were set). It worked in Chromium here, but should mirror the original attributes to be safe across browsers.
Public, unauthenticated and unthrottled while it triggers an outbound owner email per call — trivially abusable for email spam. Add a simple per-IP/email rate limit.

issues: Long service names wrap mid-word ('Data Recovery & Bac|kup') because the detail values use break-all; prefer break-words.
Uses native <select> for device/service and native <input type='date'> (browser default picker) instead of the shadcn Select/Calendar components — inconsistent with the rest of the Tech Noir styling.
Field labels use zinc-600 on #0A0A0C which is below WCAG AA contrast.

action_items: Fix brute-force keying so the 5-attempt/429 lockout works behind the multi-replica ingress (use email, or X-Forwarded-For first hop, instead of request.client.host).
Set CORS_ORIGINS to the explicit preview/production origin instead of '*' since allow_credentials=True.
Pass secure=True, samesite='none', path='/' to delete_cookie in /api/auth/logout.
Add basic rate limiting to public POST /api/bookings (email-alert abuse vector).
critical_code_review_comments: check_brute_force/record_failed_attempt rely on request.client.host, which is a proxy IP in this deployment — the security control is effectively bypassable and also lets any client lock out the real owner for 15 min.
login_attempts documents are never expired/cleaned except on success or after lockout window — add a TTL index on last_failed_at.
AdminDashboard uses `user === null` for 'checking' and `false` for logged-out; workable but a dedicated loading flag would be clearer and avoids future null/false confusion.
Responses correctly exclude Mongo _id (response_model_by_alias=False verified) and password_hash is stripped from /auth/me — good.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Run `cd /app/backend && python -m pytest tests/backend_test.py -v` — everything passes except TestBruteForce::test_lockout_after_five_failures (known ingress-IP defect above; verify the fix by hitting the PUBLIC URL, not localhost, since localhost already returns 429 on the 6th attempt). All admin UI flows (login/invalid-login/filters/mark handled/reopen/reload persistence/logout) were verified green on desktop 1920 and mobile 390 and need no re-verification unless AuthContext/AdminDashboard change. Landing page + booking POST 201 + success state + footer-owner-login-link verified. Owner email alert verified in /var/log/supervisor/backend.err.log — do not spam more submissions. Remember to delete TEST_ bookings from mongo db test_database.bookings after runs.
rca_of_the_issue: Brute-force failure RCA: the FastAPI app sits behind a Kubernetes ingress with multiple replicas. request.client.host resolves to the ingress pod IP (10.79.139.10 / 10.79.139.11 observed), so consecutive failed logins from the same external client are recorded under different identifiers, and no single counter reaches MAX_ATTEMPTS=5. Reproduction: POST /api/auth/login 6x with a wrong password against the preview URL -> all 401; the same 6 calls against http://localhost:8001 -> 6th returns 429. Mitigation: derive the identifier from the normalised email (and/or the left-most X-Forwarded-For entry) rather than request.client.host.
